raw_response:
Looking at my situation — I'm 45, been farming this land in Quzhou my whole adult life. My father farmed it before me. I have around 15 mu total, including a few mu I rent from neighbors who moved to the city.

Here in Quzhou, everybody grows wheat in the winter and corn in the summer. That's just how it is. The soil here knows these crops, I know these crops, and the market buyers in the county town take them reliably. I'm not going to try something different — cotton prices have been bad, vegetables need too much labor and you need connections to sell them well.

For wheat, I'll use the Kenong 199 variety — my neighbor switched to it two years ago and his yield was good. I'll plant it right after National Day in October. I always apply base fertilizer before sowing — diammonium phosphate plus urea — and then top-dress again at the jointing stage. I irrigate at least three times: before sowing, at overwintering, and at jointing. Sometimes a fourth time if the heading season looks dry. I'll use rotary tillage to break down the maize stubble from this past autumn.

For summer maize, I'll direct-seed Zhengdan 958 right after the wheat harvest in June — no time to waste, every day counts for heat accumulation. I won't till, just seed straight into the stubble. The summer rains usually handle most of the water, but I'll irrigate once if the seedling stage is dry. I top-dress urea around the big bell stage.

I'll keep 2 mu near the house for garlic and vegetables — that's for the family table, not for sale.
